userStories.title: [E17] Production regular expressions linear, not timed
userStories.description: Found in ARV-156 and rated by its security review: 12 production `[GeneratedRegex]` rules backtrack under a match timeout (Site.CodePattern, TopologyCodes.Code, FlightRules.Carrier and Codeshare, OutboundRules.PathAndQuery and Scope, EmailAddresses.Rule, EmailTemplates.Placeholder, CsvImportReader.Number, the Cronz JobsDashboardGuard rules), and three interpreted calls also check the clock (Email.cs:199, JobsDashboard.cs:30 and :32). A timeout is wall-clock time, so a loaded node can raise RegexMatchTimeoutException on a short input: it fails closed (DependencyOutage treats it as no outage, the handler answers 500 without detail, a check never passes), so this is robustness rather than security, but it can give a rare 500 or a failed start under load. CWEs to review: CWE-1333, CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: Every anchored production rule above runs on RegexOptions.NonBacktracking without a timeout (captures and unanchored search work on it); the linear engine is the ReDoS bound, stated in the CWE-1333 row

TopologyCodes.Code drops its lookahead for a length check (1 to 16) plus `^[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)*\z` on NonBacktracking, proven equivalent by a CsCheck property comparing old and new rules on random strings of up to 20 characters over A-Z, 0-9, '-', '\n', lowercase and non-ASCII; parity with script 0008's CHECK and varchar(16) kept

The RedactionEnricher rules keep no timeout (a timeout in a Serilog enricher would throw and could let an event out unredacted); the FloorPlanFiles backreference rule stays anchored and bounded; both are named in the CWE-1333 row with their reason
A test per rule asserts its options and infinite timeout, and each rule's accepted set is unchanged (existing tests plus a table per rule)

userStories.notes: Size XS. 2026-10-13 (ARV-173 story gate, Stryker running alongside): site-configuration.spec.ts:361 ("an oversized body answers 413 and a deeply nested one 400") failed in 88 ms on its first try and passed on Playwright's retry, with connection resets in the web server log; find why a 413 or 400 answer can surface as a reset under load and make the test robust to it without loosening what it proves. 2026-10-14: moved from Phase 1 to Phase 3 by the owner's decision (low-severity follow-ups wait until after the pilot go-live; the owner can pull one back). 2026-10-14 (ARV-176 gates): the unit total again differed by one on the same tree (5,382 in the backend gate, 5,381 in the story gate); keep the TRX of both runs to name the case. 2026-10-14 (ARV-176 backend gate, first run): BoundedProduceTests.Producer_Should_WaitForTheWindow_When_ASecondFatalErrorComesSoonAfterARecreation measured 764 ms between the two recreated clients against its 784 ms bound and passed on the single rerun. Likely a measurement error in the test, not the product: KafkaProduce.NewGeneration takes the generation's timestamp before calling the client factory, but the test reads MadeAt after the factory has built its Moq mock, so a slower first mock shrinks the measured gap. Read MadeAt before building the mock; no bound changes. 2026-10-14 (test-only fix before the checkpoint): this case is fixed. Both window tests (WaitForTheWindow and FailSendsAtOnceUntilRecreated) now measure between the producer's own generation timestamps, read back at the start of the client factory through a test clock that remembers the last timestamp it gave on that thread; no bound and no production code changed (a 40 ms stall injected into a mock's build moved the old measure to 758 to 762 ms and left the new one at 798 to 803 ms). Also (2026-10-16): Sensing.MqttTransportTests.Broker_Should_CloseSilentAndRefusedConnections_And_CapThemPerAddress failed once under the story gate's load ("Error while authenticating" after 9 s) and passed alone 3 of 3. 2026-10-16 (ARV-191 story gate, run 1): tests/api/security-baseline.spec.ts:128 ("a 2 MB body is refused with 401 before the server reads it") failed on its try and its retry with write EPIPE, 1 in 5 alone right after, then 40 of 40. Cause, probed with curl and a paced Node client: Main answers 401 before reading the body, then Kestrel closes the connection because the 2 MB Content-Length is over MaxRequestBodySize (1 MB; a 500 KB body keeps it, neither answer says Connection: close), so a client still writing the body can get EPIPE before it reads the 401; the same race as the 413 above and ARV-047's AIDX oversize upload. Fix without loosening the test: a raw-socket client that writes the body and accepts the reset only after it has read the 401 (and the same for the 413 cases), or have the server answer the oversize case with Connection: close. 2026-10-18 (ARV-082a story gate, full E2E): tests/functional/validation-capture.spec.ts:1792 ("on a portrait tablet, the desk log works on touch in English and Arabic", 800x1280) failed once at its scroll width check right after tapping the desks tab in Arabic (document.documentElement.scrollWidth > innerWidth) and passed on the retry; the story changed no web code. Likely a measurement taken before the tab's layout settles: wait for the tab panel to be shown and laid out (or poll the check) before measuring, without loosening the bound. 2026-10-18 (CI on 690f3dd): validation-capture.spec.ts:1381 ("the desk log never places a minute without Ariva's clock") stored no observation for the 18:00 minute on its first try (expected OD01 2026-10-18T18:00:00Z Serving, got none) and passed on the retry; the E2E job ran from 18:35 to 19:04 UTC; the cause is not known yet (the trace could not be fetched from the agent's session).

userStories.title: [E6] Dead letters: text PostgreSQL accepts and a per-topic relay hold
userStories.description: From the ARV-171 security review (PASS, 2026-10-13), three non-blocking findings. (1) A NUL character or a lone surrogate in a record's key, a header name or value, or the error message makes the keep fail (PostgreSQL text refuses 0x00 in message_key, and CAST AS jsonb refuses \u0000 and unpaired surrogates in the payload), so such a record still ends on ARV-166's unacknowledged path; it needs a buggy or hostile Kafka producer, which is what the unreadable path is for. (2) A dead-letter row that fails with a broker error ends the relay pass like any broker failure; a .dlq.v1 topic that hangs (its leader away while domain topics are fine) holds each attempt up to the 45 s produce bound and can delay domain events by up to 45 s repeatedly during the short backoffs. (3) The app charts set no terminationGracePeriodSeconds (Kubernetes default 30 s) and no host sets HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout (.NET default 30 s), while one in-flight message can need the rest of its retry schedule (at most 3 x 5 s), the keep (at most 10 s) and the consumer close. CWEs to review: CWE-501, CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: DeadLetters.Create replaces NUL and lone surrogates with U+FFFD in the key, header names and values and the error message, and flags the letter when it did (a header naming what was replaced, never the original bytes); OutboxKeyOf uses the digest when the key held such a character; the letter's topic, partition, offset and consumer stay exact so a replay can still fetch the original record

A .dlq.v1 row whose send fails with a broker error holds back only its topic for the rest of the relay pass instead of ending the pass, so domain rows keep draining; a domain row's failure still ends the pass as today

Unit tests: a letter with "\0" in a header and in the key is kept and its row key is the digest; a lone surrogate in the error message is replaced; a failing .dlq.v1 row leaves a domain row of the same pass sent. Integration test: a record whose key and headers carry a NUL is kept at a stop and its row read back
The residual text that names this case (ConsumeFilters, overview Producing, ADR-0018 in a new dated note, wiki 10 section 4.5a) says it is closed

userStories.title: [E18] Web requests bound to the account that started them
userStories.description: Follow-up from the ARV-104c security review (2026-10-09, Low). Api.ts recovers a 401 by refreshing the session and sending the request again. A request started by one account that is still in flight when that account signs out and another signs in on the same browser is then sent again under the second account, or its recovery signs the second account out; an MFA step-up can be shown to the second account for the first account's action. ARV-104c closed this for the capture calls only (asSubject). The server still applies the second account's permissions and site scope and audits it, so the exposure is small, but a request must never change hands. Epic: Accounts and sessions. CWEs to review: CWE-384, CWE-863, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: Api.ts request() records auth.subject when a call starts and uses it as the default for asSubject: once a different account or none is signed in, the request is not sent, not sent again after a refresh, and does not trigger the 401 recovery (no refresh, no sessionEnded, no MFA step-up)
Callers that legitimately run before a subject exists (sign-in, refresh, MFA enrolment) keep working, named explicitly in code

Playwright: a save on an administration screen held in flight across a sign-out and another account's sign-in in the same page is never sent under the second account, the second account stays signed in and sees no step-up prompt; existing session, MFA and multi-tab tests still pass

userStories.title: [E6] A host's own disposal never dead-letters a valid message, and the broker probe names no topic
userStories.description: From the ARV-165 security review (PASS, 2026-10-14), two low findings. (F2) The stop budget covers the retry schedule and the 10 s keep but not the consumer's own time per attempt: when attempts are slow at a stop (a database stall at Npgsql's 30 s command timeout), MassTransit's stop wait can end with a message still in its retries; the host disposes its container while the bus keeps stopping in the background, the later attempts fail with ObjectDisposedException, and the final attempt keeps the dead letter, so a valid event lands in the dead-letter topic (a replay is needed), or is faulted when the database is away too. Wiki 10 section 4.5a states the case and the replay meanwhile. (Probe) KafkaProduce.BrokersAnswerAsync calls GetMetadata(timeout), which asks for every topic on the cluster; on a large or shared cluster the reply is large. A metadata request that names one topic is not the answer: Confluent.Kafka 2.15.1 documents allow.auto.create.topics as true by default for producer-type clients (the admin client is one), so naming a missing topic can create it with the broker's defaults, AMAN's topics included (seen in ARV-176's first baseline). CWEs to review: CWE-400, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: A failure caused by the host's own disposal while its endpoint stops (ObjectDisposedException from the host's services, or an equivalent signal) does not dead-letter the message: the record is left unacknowledged so it is delivered again after the restart, without opening the ARV-166 skip (prove the checkpointer cannot pass it)

The readiness probe names no topic: it uses IAdminClient.DescribeClusterAsync on the producer's handle within the same 3 s bound, single-flight and reused for 1 s, and still reports Degraded within its bound when no broker answers. A metadata request naming one topic is not used (it lets a broker with auto.create.topics.enable create the topic with broker defaults). If DescribeCluster proves unsuitable, keep GetMetadata(timeout) for all topics, whose cost is bounded at one request a second per pod

Ariva's producer and admin client configurations set AllowAutoCreateTopics = false (KafkaClientConfig), with a test proving that a send or a metadata read for a missing topic does not create it, so no Ariva client can create a topic implicitly whatever the cluster's setting; the relay and Ingest treat the resulting unknown-topic failure as the row's own failure
Unit tests for both; an integration test where a slow attempt outlasts the bus's stop wait and the message comes back after the restart instead of reaching the dead-letter topic
Wiki 10 section 4.5a no longer describes the edge case as open

userStories.title: [E4] Sensing resends: late receipt-timed resends and bounded declarative names
userStories.description: Two low findings from ARV-174 (2026-10-14). (1) The engineer's: a receipt-timed message resent more than about three minutes after the first (the queue engine's RecentBatches window) is applied again live while the archive keeps it once (its id window is three days), so live and replayed counts differ; no shipped mapping stamps crossings at receipt, so the pilot is not affected. (2) The ARV-174 security review's recommendation 1: a declarative mapping that reads a name or id from the group (^) or payload ($) level makes DeclarativeMapper.State.Name and Id call GetString() per item, a fresh copy each time (2,000 items x up to about 500 KB, roughly 1 GB), and the batch id's encoding would copy and sort it again; latent, since no shipped mapping does this. userStories.title: [E12] A queue zone's direction: one rule for the arrival wave projection, the staffing lanes and desks, and the desk term
userStories.description: From the ARV-191 security review (2026-10-16). Since ARV-191 the arrival wave projection links a queue zone to a lane only through desks of an Immigration checkpoint on the queue zone's level. The staffing recommendation and the throughput desk term use other rules: StaffingInputs.LanesAsync (and its CTEs) admits an emigration queue with a lane category on a level that has an Immigration checkpoint as an arrivals-hall lane, so SiteStaffing splits the arrivals wave with it and recommends desks for it; DeskTermSource (the F8 desk term) counts Immigration and Emigration desks sharing a lane code on a level in n_open. So at a site whose arrivals level also has an Emigration checkpoint, one PredictedNowcast evaluation takes its arrivals from Immigration desks only and its throughput from both (overstating throughput, under-predicting the breach), and the staffing panel shows a recommendation for an emigration queue. Counting Emigration desks in the desk term is right for departures queues, so the fix is not to copy the Immigration-only filter there: give a queue zone a direction (an explicit link to its checkpoint, or one derived from its service zones' desks' checkpoints with mixed links refused at publish) and apply one rule in the projection, the staffing lanes and desks, and the desk term. Correctness, not an exposure: every output involved is border-only. CWEs to review: CWE-863 (a check that the border-only pins hold).

userStories.title: [E21] Display player measures elapsed time on a monotonic clock
userStories.description: Security review of ARV-143b (Low): the passenger display player measures how old its last good board is, and so whether the board is stale and whether a plan's untilUtc has passed, with Date.now(). If the kiosk's wall clock jumps backwards while it is offline, the board is not counted stale and the plan does not expire until the clock catches up. The queue board's staleness used the same pattern before ARV-143b.
acceptanceCriteria: The player measures the time since its last good board with performance.now() (a monotonic clock), and the server's clock as serverUtc plus that elapsed time
A Playwright test that moves the page's wall clock back (page.clock) while the network is down still shows the neutral message and instructions once the stale threshold has passed
node scripts/verify.mjs web passes; the display player functional specs pass
userStories.notes: Size S. Recorded 2026-10-18 with ARV-143b under the owner's standing decision (low-severity follow-ups wait for Phase 3 unless needed before the pilot; the owner can pull one back). 2026-10-18 (found by the PR #67 proof of play test, ARV-144): the player sets its estimate of the server's clock from each board's serverUtc as the board arrives, so a board that reaches it later than the one before (a slow server or network) moves the estimate back by the difference. A plan that had run out then plays again for those seconds, and the advertisement on screen is reported twice with nearly the same start (the server refuses the overlap, so it is under-reported, never over-claimed). Reproduced with every other board 7 seconds late. Keep the estimate from moving backwards (for example the largest serverUtc offset seen within the last minute), and let the board stamp serverUtc when it is composed rather than when it starts (SvcDisplayBoard reads the clock before its queries).

userStories.title: [E0] The web pod serves a renewed certificate without a restart
userStories.description: Found while building ARV-082b: in k8s-prd the web pod's nginx serves TLS on 3443 from ariva-web-tls and reads the certificate only when it starts, so a renewed certificate takes effect at the pod's next restart (every release restarts it). If no release or restart happens before the old certificate expires, the ingress, which verifies the pod against the cluster CA, refuses the web backend and the screens go down. The API hosts reload theirs on their own (Kestrel watches the files). CWEs to review: CWE-295 (closest: CWE-287 row), CWE-400.
acceptanceCriteria: A renewed ariva-web-tls (the kubelet's ..data swap of the secret volume) is served by the running web pod within a stated bound, without a restart and without dropping the connections it holds; or, if the owner prefers, the chart restarts the web Deployment on a renewal through a mechanism the chart test enforces
An alert fires before the certificate a pod actually serves expires (the API hosts' and the web pod's), as part of the ARV-125b monitoring
A throwaway container test shows the new certificate served after the swap; tests/chart-security.mjs covers whatever the chart adds
node scripts/verify.mjs quick passes; docs and wiki pages affected by the change are updated (node scripts/verify.mjs docs passes)
security-reviewer verdict PASS recorded in backlog/progress.md for the CWEs listed in this story
userStories.notes: Size S. Recorded 2026-10-18 with ARV-082b under the owner's standing decision (low-severity follow-ups wait for Phase 3 unless needed before the pilot; the owner can pull one back). Until then the deployment guide tells the operator to restart the web Deployment after a renewal, or to renew well inside the release cadence. Related residual from ARV-082b: api-cronz and api-integration run one replica in prd (HPA minimum 1), so during their own certificate's rebind new connections can fail for up to about 5 s; a second replica would remove it.
